title: VoiceVision RAG - Integrating Visual Document Intelligence with Voice Response — Suman Debnath, AWS
talk_summary: Suman Debnath (AWS) explains ColPali-style vision-based document retrieval: treat each PDF page as an image, embed page patches with a vision model, and use late-interaction (MaxSim) scoring to rank pages for a text query, then feed top pages to a multimodal LLM. He wraps the retrieval in a lightweight Strands agent with custom tools (retrieve, image reader, speak) and demos MCP integration.

takeaways.what_they_do: They collapse a multi-cell notebook pipeline into one decorated function (retrieve_from_qdrant) exposed as a tool, then let a minimal agent (model + tools, no scaffolding) decide when to call it and when to call an image-reader tool for the final answer.
takeaways.evidence_quote: our tool is not the default one but the tool that we have defined... just by importing tool and just use that as a decorator on top of your function

takeaways.what_they_do: Strands is 'model first': they show the same agent working with the system prompt deleted, relying on the model to reason and route to tools; they also note tool specs (persona) are the deterministic place for behavior, not the prompt.
takeaways.evidence_quote: you can simply remove the system prompt you will still get the right answer

takeaways.technique: Retrieve pages, not chunks, via late interaction
takeaways.what_they_do: Instead of OCR-splitting text/tables/images, embed whole pages as patch vectors and score a query by summing per-token max similarity (MaxSim) across patches, returning top-N pages to the LLM.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we just take a sum the maximum numbers of each rows and if let's say that is 2.58 that means this query has a score of 2.58 for page number one
takeaways.numbers: 128-dim embeddings; ~15 patches/page in demo; top-5 pages retrieved

takeaways.technique: Cheapest-architecture-first, escalate only on convoluted data
takeaways.what_they_do: Speaker explicitly recommends starting with the cheap traditional pipeline and only moving to the heavy vision model when the data genuinely requires visual understanding, because indexing is expensive.
takeaways.evidence_quote: I would recommend not to start with this start with the traditional technique because that is more effective um cost effective

takeaways.technique: Batch-size caution for heavy local jobs
takeaways.what_they_do: He crashed his laptop running a vision model at batch size 12 on 16GB; recommends starting at 2-3 and notes GPU strongly preferred over CPU for vision workloads.
takeaways.evidence_quote: if it's your personal laptop make sure that the batch size is very small otherwise it will it will crash
